record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: In hybrid interfaces between a two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnet such as Fe3GeTe2 and a three-dimensional non-van-der-Waals ferromagnet such as Ni, what are the interfacial spin textures and couplings, how does a possible oxidized Fe3GeTe2 interlayer affect them, and how would any resulting exchange bias influence the magnetic properties of the metal layer and spin transport across the interface?

evidence.quote: However, the exact nature of the interfacial spins (i.e., their spin textures) and their couplings to Fe spins located within each layer are unknown in these hybrid systems.

Further studies are needed to clarify this effect. Since oxidized Fe3GeTe2 flakes could exhibit an EB effect, it would be necessary to create oxidized Fe3GeTe2/Ni heterostructures and investigate impacts of EB on the magnetic property of the Ni layer, as well as on the spin transport across the Fe3GeTe2/Ni interface.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hybrid magnetic heterostructure formed by interfacing a two-dimensional van der Waals itinerant ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT), with Curie temperature in the bulk near 220 K and out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy, with a three-dimensional non-van-der-Waals ferromagnetic metal such as Ni. Address the following questions:

(a) Determine the interfacial spin textures at the FGT/Ni interface: characterize the orientation, magnitude, and possible non-collinearity (e.g., canting, spirals, skyrmionic features) of the magnetic moments of the Fe atoms in the topmost FGT layer and of the Ni atoms in the first atomic plane of the metal, and identify the dominant exchange couplings (sign, strength, anisotropic and Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya components) between the interfacial Fe spins and (i) the Fe spins within deeper FGT layers and (ii) the Ni spins within the metallic film.

(b) Suppose an ultrathin oxidized FGT interlayer (denoted O-FGT) forms spontaneously between FGT and Ni, and that this oxide layer can support antiferromagnetic order. Determine how the presence of such an O-FGT interlayer modifies the interfacial spin textures and the couplings identified in (a), and whether it produces an exchange bias (a horizontal shift of the magnetic hysteresis loop after field cooling) at the FGT/Ni interface.

(c) Quantify how any exchange bias arising in (b) affects the magnetic properties of the Ni layer (coercivity, anisotropy, domain structure, blocking temperature dependence on Ni thickness) and the spin transport across the FGT/O-FGT/Ni interface (spin polarization, interfacial spin-mixing conductance, magnetoresistance, and spin-torque efficiencies).
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search shows extensive recent work on exchange bias in Fe3GeTe2-based heterostructures (with CrCl3, FePS3, CrPS4, MnPS3, and naturally oxidized FGT surfaces), but no studies were found that directly characterize the interfacial spin textures, couplings, and exchange-bias-induced spin-transport effects at FGT/Ni hybrid interfaces or at oxidized-FGT/Ni interfaces. The specific questions therefore remain open.

status_evidence.title: Harnessing Van der Waals CrPS4 and Surface Oxides for Nonmonotonic Preset Field Induced Exchange Bias in Fe3GeTe2
status_evidence.snippet: Exchange bias is observed in naturally oxidized Fe3GeTe2 due to AFM ordering in the surface oxide layer.
status_evidence.claim: Oxidized FGT surfaces can produce exchange bias, supporting the relevance of the O-FGT interlayer scenario, but FGT/Ni systems are not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias in van der Waals CrCl3/Fe3GeTe2 Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Exchange bias studied in CrCl3/FGT vdW heterostructures.
status_evidence.claim: Studies focus on FGT with antiferromagnetic vdW partners, not with 3D ferromagnetic metals such as Ni.

status_evidence.title: Manipulating exchange bias in 2D magnetic heterojunction for high-performance robust memory applications
status_evidence.snippet: Exchange bias in 2D magnetic heterojunctions for memory applications.
status_evidence.claim: Recent investigations of EB in vdW heterojunctions do not include FGT/Ni interfaces.
